features.summary: Execution: how a plan runs in the browser. Boot starts each owner's handlers in plan order; a handler runs one run, a state machine whose steps run in the trigger's turn until one awaits, and only the closed awaited steps C# marks wait: a send, a Confirm, a hub's invoke and send, and a method declared MethodAsync, whose rejection stops the run. Steps before the first await run in the vendor's turn, so a payload write there reaches the vendor, and C# refuses one after it on the path the handler runs. A stop unwinds the run's frames innermost first, each request running its Finally layers once; a replace or a dispose aborts the run's blocks and runs no route; a join waits for every block's tail. Data read where a member is absent reads the start System.Text.Json binds for it, stops where the binding cannot make the holder or the holder lacks what its type requires, and a path value that reads nothing stops its request before it is sent. Main drops a call's promise and refuses no late payload write; the redesign logs a rejection and goes on, reads data's members as optional, and ends no run at dispose.

sentences.text: Pure sync reactions must return before Syncfusion inspects mutable event args
Two-phase wiring: wire all non-page-ready listeners first, then execute page-ready.
if (isPromise(completion)) return completion.then(() => runFrom(statements, index + 1, scope));
objects.subscribe(handler.on, handler.path, handler.event, payload => runHandler(handler, payload, objects), owner);
if (isMissing(value)) throw new Error(`[alis] route param "${name}" evaluated to null; cannot build URL`);
G.Let(response, G.Call(G.Obj(scope.Objects.Http()), PathMembers.Required, "send", SendArgument(method, input, scope)), awaits: true),

A pipeline runs as one run, a state machine whose driver alone continues on a promise: its steps run in the trigger's turn until one awaits, a stop unwinds its frames innermost first, running each request's Finally layers, and ends its own handler only.
A write to the trigger's payload itself after an awaited step, on the path the handler runs, is refused where the view renders, and a write to an object the payload holds runs.

A handler's policy, overlap, replace or skip, decides what a trigger does while its run is in flight; replace and a dispose abort the run's blocks' signals, and each Finally layer whose WhileLoading completed runs once.

features.oracle: The spec itself where the framework is the authority: spec/Core/Run.tla, Lanes.tla and Absence.tla, whose invariants TLC checks, and Request.tla's states, which Run.tla runs as frames; ECMA-262's promise jobs for what runs in a turn; the DOM and Fetch Standards' AbortSignal and fetch, pinned in spec/probes (abort-signal-keeps-first-reason, fetch-aborted-signal-sends-nothing); System.Text.Json 10's binding for a data member's start (core-stj-empty-object-start, core-stj-populate-start, core-json-nested-start); and EJ2 33.1.47's declared return types and payloads (ej2-methods-returning-promise, ej2-filtering-args-members).

promises.page: A bed board whose Find a free bed button sends GET /beds/free, which answers {"bed": null} when the ward is full; its success route sends GET /beds/{bedId} with bedId read from the answer's Bed.Id. That second request's WhileLoading writes Opening into bed-status, its busy indicator is bed-busy, its success route writes the bed's name into bed-name and its Finally writes Closed into bed-status.
promises.gesture: With the ward full, click Find a free bed.
promises.outcome: bed-status reads Closed, bed-busy never shows, bed-name stays empty, and only the GET /beds/free request is sent.
promises.opposite: With bed East 4 free, the same click shows bed-busy while the second request is in flight, then East 4 in bed-name and Closed in bed-status.
promises.defect: The missing path value throws inside the send, as the redesign's route fill does (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/plugins/http.ts:83 at 65fdf118d), so the Finally never runs and bed-status keeps Opening; or the request is sent with an empty segment and its answer shows in bed-name.

promises.page: A dose census, a test component whose doses property holds the ward's doses as data the app's options wrote under WhenWritingDefault, and an on-call board, a test component whose nurse property holds data that lacks callback. Dose declares Refills, an int, and Unit, a string initialized to mg; OnCallNurse initializes Callback to switchboard. Digoxin's refills are 0 and its unit mcg, Heparin's refills 0 and its unit null, so Heparin's data holds neither, and Aspirin's refills 2 and its unit mg. Count doses with no refills left writes the count of doses whose Refills is 0 into refills-count; Count doses measured in mg writes the count of doses whose Unit is mg into mg-count; Show Heparin's unit writes the Unit of the dose Find(d => d.Drug == "Heparin") returns into heparin-unit; Show callback writes the nurse's Callback into nurse-callback.
promises.gesture: Click Count doses with no refills left, Count doses measured in mg, Show Heparin's unit and Show callback.
promises.outcome: refills-count reads 2, mg-count reads 2, heparin-unit reads mg and nurse-callback reads switchboard.
promises.opposite: With Heparin's refills 1 and its unit mL, refills-count reads 1, mg-count reads 1 and heparin-unit reads mL; with the nurse's data holding callback x4410, nurse-callback reads x4410.
promises.defect: An absent member reads nothing, as the redesign reads data's members as optional (Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Values/Target.cs:80 at 65fdf118d), so refills-count reads 0, mg-count reads 1, and heparin-unit and nurse-callback stay empty; or the browser picks a start by the member's shape, so heparin-unit shows an empty text.

promises.page: The dose census, whose Dose declares Shelf, a Storage it populates ([JsonObjectCreationHandling(Populate)]), Locker, a getter-only Storage, and Spare, a Storage it replaces, each initialized by Dose to a Storage whose Place is fridge, where Storage's own initializer sets Place to cupboard; Heparin's data holds shelf, locker and spare each as {}. Show Heparin's stores writes Heparin's Shelf.Place, Locker.Place and Spare.Place into shelf-place, locker-place and spare-place.
promises.gesture: Click Show Heparin's stores.
promises.outcome: shelf-place reads fridge, locker-place reads fridge and spare-place reads cupboard.
promises.opposite: With each of Heparin's three stores holding place Ward 4, shelf-place, locker-place and spare-place read Ward 4.
promises.defect: One start per type, as the redesign builds a start from the type alone (Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Validation/ModelDefaults.cs:126 at 65fdf118d), so all three read cupboard; or an absent member reads nothing and the three stay empty.

promises.page: The dose census, whose Dose declares Constructor, a string? whose JSON name is constructor, which none of its four doses' data holds. Count doses with no maker writes the count of doses whose Constructor is null into maker-count.
promises.gesture: Click Count doses with no maker.
promises.outcome: maker-count reads 4.
promises.opposite: With Heparin's data holding constructor Ward pharmacy, maker-count reads 3.
promises.defect: The read finds what every object inherits, the Object function, at constructor, so no dose's Constructor is null and maker-count reads 0.

promises.page: The dose census, whose Aspirin batch holds lot L-17 and expiry 2027-01 and whose Heparin batch lacks lot, which DoseBatch declares [JsonRequired]; a seal lacking its breaker, where DoseSeal has only a private constructor; and a delivery lacking its site, where DoseDelivery is [JsonPolymorphic]. Beside it, an on-call board whose nurse's pager holds a list where OnCallNurse declares an object, and a ward board, a test component whose census property holds data whose count member the component set to a promise. List batch expiries, List seal breakers, List delivery sites, Show the pager's number and Show the census count each write a status into census-status (Listing expiries, Listing breakers, Listing sites, Paging, Counting) and then write their read into census-list, pager-number or census-count; Show Aspirin's batch expiry writes Aspirin's expiry into aspirin-expiry.
promises.gesture: Click List batch expiries, List seal breakers, List delivery sites, Show the pager's number, Show the census count and Show Aspirin's batch expiry in turn.
promises.outcome: census-status reads each button's status in turn, census-list holds no row, pager-number and census-count stay empty, and aspirin-expiry reads 2027-01.
promises.opposite: With Heparin's batch holding lot L-12, the seal holding breaker R. Okafor, the delivery holding site Ward 4, the pager holding an object whose number is x4410 and the census count holding 42, each button writes its read after its status: the expiries, the breaker, the sites, x4410 and 42.
promises.defect: An absent member reads nothing and the pipeline goes on, as the redesign reads data's members as optional (Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Values/Target.cs:80 at 65fdf118d), so census-list shows empty rows and pager-number and census-count show nothing; or a start the binding cannot make, a new seal or a delivery of the declared type, is read in the member's place; or the promise is written as text.

promises.page: A dose census on an app whose JSON options set RespectRequiredConstructorParameters, where Dose is a record whose constructor takes Drug and Ward: Heparin's data lacks ward, and Digoxin's holds both and lacks refills. Count doses with no refills left writes Counting refills into census-status and then the count into census-count, which reads unknown until then; Show Digoxin's refills left writes Digoxin's Refills into digoxin-refills.
promises.gesture: Click Count doses with no refills left, then Show Digoxin's refills left.
promises.outcome: census-status reads Counting refills, census-count keeps unknown, and digoxin-refills reads 0.
promises.opposite: On the same app with RespectRequiredConstructorParameters off, Count doses with no refills left writes the count into census-count.
promises.defect: The missing constructor parameter goes unchecked, so the count reads Heparin's Refills as its start and census-count shows a number; or the option stops every read through a dose, so digoxin-refills stays empty.

promises.page: An infusion pump page. The pump, a test component, declares Check as a MethodAsync it settles by its own Finish the check and Fail the check buttons, Measure as a MethodAsync<PumpReading> that resolves to a reading of volume 125 with a limit of 750, LastCheck as a MethodAsync<PumpCheck?> that resolves to nothing, and Caption, a method that shows (no caption) when it receives null and the text it receives otherwise; an older pump declares Measure as a MethodAsync<PumpReading> whose method returns a plain reading of volume 90. Run the self-test writes Testing into check-status, awaits Check and writes Self-test passed; Measure the volume writes the reading's volume into volume; Show the remote volume limit writes the reading's limit into volume-limit; Measure the older pump's volume writes its volume into older-volume; Caption with the last check passes LastCheck's result to Caption.
promises.gesture: Click Run the self-test, then Finish the check; click Run the self-test again, then Fail the check; then click Measure the volume, Show the remote volume limit, Measure the older pump's volume and Caption with the last check.
promises.outcome: check-status reads Testing until Finish the check and Self-test passed after it; after the second run and Fail the check it reads Testing; volume reads 125, volume-limit 750, older-volume 90, and the pump's caption (no caption).
promises.opposite: Before any click on Finish the check, check-status keeps Testing; with Measure resolving to a volume of 60, volume reads 60.
promises.defect: The step after the call runs in the call's turn, as main drops a call's promise (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/execution/reactions/execute.ts:181 at 623dd4a27), so Self-test passed shows before Finish the check and after Fail the check; or a resolution to nothing reaches Caption as undefined, which shows undefined; or the older pump's plain value stops the pipeline, so older-volume stays empty.

promises.page: A dose census index with the link Count Ruth's charters, to a census page whose Dose declares Charter, a Charterer its own [JsonConverter] writes as the charterer's name, and whose Count button writes Count(d => d.Charter.Name == "Ruth") over the doses into charter-count.
promises.gesture: On the census index, click Count Ruth's charters.
promises.outcome: The census page is refused where the view renders with "'d.Charter.Name' reads past 'd.Charter', which its own JSON converter writes, so the browser holds what the converter writes, not its members; read 'd.Charter' itself, or read past it on the server."
promises.opposite: With Charter written by the app's options, the page renders, and Count writes 2 into charter-count, the doses Ruth charters.
promises.defect: The read is written past the converter's text, so the page renders and Count writes 0, since the browser's charter is a text with no Name.

promises.page: The census index's link Find Ruth's dose, to a census page whose Dose declares Charter as above, and whose Show the charter button writes the field d => d.Charter.Name of the dose Find(d => d.Drug == "Heparin") returns into found-charter.
promises.gesture: On the census index, click Find Ruth's dose.
promises.outcome: The census page is refused where the view renders with "'d.Charter.Name' reads past 'd.Charter', which its own JSON converter writes, so the browser holds what the converter writes, not its members; read 'd.Charter' itself, or read past it on the server."
promises.opposite: With Charter written by the app's options, the page renders, and Show the charter writes Ruth into found-charter.
promises.defect: The field is read past the converter's text, so the page renders and found-charter stays empty.

promises.page: A care plan page whose NativeDrawer holds the care plan form and opens from Edit care plan. The drawer's BeforeClose handler, when ClosedBy is the close button, writes the event's Cancel, then asks with Confirm "Discard the unsaved care plan?" and, on Yes, calls the drawer's Close, whose own BeforeClose writes no Cancel.
promises.gesture: Click Edit care plan, click the drawer's close button, then click Yes.
promises.outcome: While the dialog asks, the drawer stays open; after Yes it closes.
promises.opposite: Clicking No instead of Yes keeps the drawer open after the dialog closes.
promises.defect: The drawer reads Cancel after the handler's first await, so it closes while the dialog asks and Yes closes nothing.

promises.page: A medication order page whose Start infusion button sends POST /orders with the busy indicator order-busy; its success route writes Priming into prime-status, awaits the pump's Prime, a MethodAsync the pump settles by its own Finish priming and Fail priming buttons, then writes Primed; the request's Finally writes Finished into order-status.
promises.gesture: Click Start infusion, then the pump's Fail priming.
promises.outcome: prime-status keeps Priming, order-status reads Finished and order-busy hides.
promises.opposite: With Finish priming instead of Fail priming, prime-status reads Primed, order-status reads Finished and order-busy hides.
promises.defect: The call's promise is not awaited, as main drops it (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/execution/reactions/execute.ts:181 at 623dd4a27), so Primed shows before the pump settles; or the stop skips the Finally, so order-status stays empty and order-busy stays shown.

promises.page: The resident record whose tab slot holds the resident card partial. The card's Refresh sends GET /residents/7, with the busy indicator ward-busy outside the slot and a success route that writes Refreshed into ward-status, also outside the slot; the record's Close card button unloads the slot. The harness gates GET /residents/7 (Composition.tla's Answer).
promises.gesture: Click Refresh; once the harness reports GET /residents/7 held, click Close card, then release it.
promises.outcome: ward-busy hides when the card closes, and ward-status stays empty after the release.
promises.opposite: Without Close card, the release writes Refreshed into ward-status and hides ward-busy.
promises.defect: Dispose ends no run in flight, as the redesign's owner only runs its disposers (Alis.Reactive.Assets/runtime/objects/owner.ts:32-40 at 65fdf118d), so Refreshed shows after the release; or the busy target is held past the dispose, so ward-busy stays shown.

promises.page: The component bench's ConformanceComponent with its own search box: its Raised payload carries the box's text, the component reads the payload's WriteOnlyText when its listeners return and shows it in its note line, and the payload method Fill shows the names it is given in its list. The Raised handler writes the payload's WriteOnlyText as Filtered, sends GET /items with the payload's Text in the query, and in the success route calls the payload's Fill with the answer's names; the endpoint answers Alpha and Alpine for al, and Beta for be.
promises.gesture: Type al into the component's search box and click its Raise button.
promises.outcome: The note line reads Filtered and the list shows Alpha and Alpine.
promises.opposite: With be typed, the list shows Beta.
promises.defect: The call to Fill after the send is refused or dropped as a write to the payload, so the list shows no name; or WriteOnlyText is written after the component read it, so the note line stays empty.

promises.page: A vitals monitor, a test component whose Raise a noted alarm button raises its alarm with the patient it holds, a live object whose status the monitor shows, resting until written. The alarm handler awaits the desk's Acknowledge, a MethodAsync the monitor's Confirm the acknowledgement button settles, then writes acknowledged into the patient's Status.
promises.gesture: Click Raise a noted alarm, then Confirm the acknowledgement.
promises.outcome: The monitor's patient reads resting until the confirmation and acknowledged after it.
promises.opposite: Without Confirm the acknowledgement, the patient keeps resting.
promises.defect: Every write after an awaited step is refused where the view renders, as a write to the payload itself is, so the page does not render; or the write lands on a copy of the payload, so the patient keeps resting.

promises.page: Three vitals monitors, each a test component that raises its alarm from its own Raise a noted alarm button and, once its listeners return, shows cancelled when the alarm's cancel holds true and sounding otherwise, then moves the alarm from bed 4 to bed 6. The first monitor's handler writes the alarm's Cancel and Acknowledging into ack-status, awaits the desk's Acknowledge, which the monitor's Confirm the acknowledgement settles, then writes acknowledged into the alarm's patient, calls the alarm's Silence, which the monitor shows as silenced, and writes the alarm's bed and Acknowledged into ack-bed and ack-status. The second monitor has two handlers: the first awaits the desk's Acknowledge at once, and the second, written after it, writes the alarm's Cancel before its own await. The third monitor's handler writes nothing to its alarm.
promises.gesture: Click Raise a noted alarm on each monitor, then Confirm the acknowledgement on the first.
promises.outcome: The first monitor shows cancelled and ack-status reads Acknowledging; after the confirmation its patient reads acknowledged, it shows silenced, ack-bed reads 6 and ack-status reads Acknowledged; the second monitor shows cancelled and the third sounding.
promises.opposite: Before the confirmation, the first monitor's patient reads resting, it shows not silenced and ack-bed stays empty.
promises.defect: The handler continues after a microtask, so the first monitor reads no cancel and shows sounding; or the second handler waits for the first one's await, so its Cancel misses the second monitor's turn and it shows sounding; or a read after the await reads a snapshot of the payload, so ack-bed reads 4.

promises.page: A vitals monitor whose alarm handler, when the alarm is noted, awaits the desk's Acknowledge, and in its Else writes the alarm's Cancel; the monitor shows cancelled or sounding once its listeners return. On the monitors index, the link Late cancel opens a page whose handler writes the Cancel after that When.
promises.gesture: Click Raise an unnoted alarm, then Raise a noted alarm, then click Late cancel on the monitors index.
promises.outcome: After the unnoted alarm the monitor shows cancelled and after the noted one sounding, and the Late cancel page is refused where the view renders with "A write to the event's payload after an awaited step reaches no vendor: write it before the first request, Confirm or async method."
promises.opposite: With the late Cancel moved before the When, the Late cancel page renders and its unnoted alarm shows cancelled.
promises.defect: The C# counts any await in the handler as before every write, so the first page is refused; or the Else runs after the monitor's turn, so the unnoted alarm sounds; or the late write passes the render and reaches no vendor.

promises.page: A vitals monitor whose alarm handler awaits the desk's Acknowledge when the alarm is critical, writes Watching into monitor-note in an ElseIf when it is noted, and in its Else writes the alarm's Cancel. On the monitors index, the link Cancel after an awaited check opens a page whose ElseIf condition awaits the desk's IsStaffed, a MethodAsync<bool>, before the same Else.
promises.gesture: Click Raise an unnoted alarm, then click Cancel after an awaited check on the monitors index.
promises.outcome: The monitor shows cancelled, and the second page is refused where the view renders with "A write to the event's payload after an awaited step reaches no vendor: write it before the first request, Confirm or async method."
promises.opposite: With the ElseIf's condition reading the alarm's Noted member instead of IsStaffed, the second page renders and its unnoted alarm shows cancelled.
promises.defect: The Else reads the state before the ElseIf's condition, so the second page renders and its Cancel reaches no vendor; or an await in a sibling branch refuses the Else, so the first page is refused.

promises.page: The admission screen whose Admit button sends POST /admissions, taking no defaults. Its success route appends Admitted to the log, sends POST /beds and then appends Bed assigned; the admission's Finally appends Finally, its Chained appends Chained, and the step after the request appends After. The harness gates POST /beds (Lanes.tla's SettleTheTail).
promises.gesture: Click Admit; once the harness reports POST /beds held, check the log, then release it.
promises.outcome: Before the release the log reads Admitted; after it the log reads Admitted, Bed assigned, Finally, Chained, After.
promises.opposite: With the route sending no second request, the log reads Admitted, Bed assigned, Finally, Chained, After once the admission answers, with nothing held.
promises.defect: Finally, Chained and the step after run once the route reaches its first awaited step, as a join over the route's first promise alone would, so the log reads Admitted, Finally, Chained, After before the release and Bed assigned after it.

promises.page: The residents screen whose Refresh button, under replace, sends GET /roster; its success route sends GET /shifts and writes shifts shown into roster-status. The shifts request's Finally appends inner finally to the log, the roster request's Finally appends outer finally, and the app's request defaults' Finally appends defaults finally for each request. The harness gates the first run's GET /shifts (Lanes.tla's Respond).
promises.gesture: Click Refresh; once the harness reports the first run's GET /shifts held, click Refresh again; then release it.
promises.outcome: After the second click the log reads inner finally, defaults finally, outer finally, defaults finally, each once, and after the release the first run writes no shifts shown.
promises.opposite: Under overlap, the second click starts a second run beside the first, and after the release the first run writes shifts shown before its Finally layers run.
promises.defect: The abort runs the outer Finally before the inner one, or the defaults' layer once for both requests, so the log reads another order; or the aborted run's route goes on and writes shifts shown after the release.

promises.page: The residents screen whose Load board button runs Parallel: one branch sends GET /residents, whose success route sends GET /allergies; the other branch sends GET /staff. The step after Parallel writes Board ready into board-status. The harness gates GET /allergies (Lanes.tla's Settle).
promises.gesture: Click Load board; once the harness reports GET /allergies held, check board-status, then release it.
promises.outcome: board-status stays empty while the allergies request is in flight, and reads Board ready after the release.
promises.opposite: With the residents route sending no request, Board ready shows once both branches answer, with nothing held.
promises.defect: The join waits for each branch's request and not for its route's own request, so Board ready shows before the release.

promises.page: An app whose request defaults' WhileLoading awaits the session plugin's Renew, a MethodAsync. A residents index with the link Discharge Ada, to a discharge page whose drawer's BeforeClose handler sends POST /discharge with a WhileLoading that writes the event's Cancel.
promises.gesture: On the residents index, click Discharge Ada.
promises.outcome: The discharge page is refused where the view renders with "A write to the event's payload after an awaited step reaches no vendor: write it before the first request, Confirm or async method."
promises.opposite: With the defaults' WhileLoading awaiting nothing, the discharge page renders, and closing its drawer keeps it open while the discharge is sent.
promises.defect: The C# reads the request's own WhileLoading as in the vendor's turn whatever the defaults await, so the page renders and its drawer closes, since the Cancel reaches the drawer after Renew's await.

promises.page: An admissions page whose Admit button sends POST /admissions; its success route sends POST /beds, then appends after beds, and the beds request's success route reads the bed board's Capacity, a declared property the page's bed board lacks. The beds request's Finally appends inner finally, the admission's Finally outer finally, the app's request defaults' Finally defaults finally for each request, and the step after the admission appends after admission.
promises.gesture: Click Admit.
promises.outcome: The log reads inner finally, defaults finally, outer finally, defaults finally, and neither after beds nor after admission.
promises.opposite: With the bed board holding Capacity, the log reads inner finally, defaults finally, after beds, outer finally, defaults finally, after admission.
promises.defect: A stop unwinds past a request frame without its Finally layers, so the log lacks inner finally; or the stop ends the inner route alone, so after beds appears.

promises.page: A roster page whose Refresh button, under replace, sends GET /roster and writes its round, 1 then 2, into each line it appends. The request's own WhileLoading awaits the pump's Prime, a MethodAsync whose every pending call the pump settles by its Finish priming button, then shows roster-busy; its Finally appends finally, the app's request defaults' Finally defaults finally, and its success route route, each with the round.
promises.gesture: Click Refresh, click Refresh again before Finish priming, then click Finish priming.
promises.outcome: After the second click the log reads defaults finally 1 and roster-busy stays hidden; after Finish priming the log reads defaults finally 1, route 2, finally 2, defaults finally 2.
promises.opposite: Under overlap, the second click leaves round 1 running, and after Finish priming the log holds route 1, finally 1 and defaults finally 1 as well.
promises.defect: The aborted request runs its own Finally although its WhileLoading never completed, so finally 1 appears; or the defaults' Finally is skipped with it, so defaults finally 1 is missing; or round 1's WhileLoading goes on after its await, so roster-busy shows before round 2 sends and route 1 appears.

promises.page: A roster page whose Refresh button, under replace, sends GET /roster and writes its round into each line it appends. The request's Finally appends finally start, awaits the pump's Flush, a MethodAsync the pump settles by its Finish flushing button, then appends finally end; the app's request defaults' Finally appends defaults finally, and the step after the request appends after.
promises.gesture: Click Refresh, and once finally start 1 shows click Refresh again, then click Finish flushing each time the pump asks.
promises.outcome: finally end 1 shows once, after the first Finish flushing, followed by defaults finally 1, and after 1 never shows.
promises.opposite: Under overlap, the second click leaves round 1 running, and after Finish flushing the log holds after 1.
promises.defect: The replace ends the old Finally at its await, so finally end 1 never shows; or the old Finally runs again for the new run, so finally end 1 shows twice; or the step after the old request runs, so after 1 shows.

promises.page: A ward page whose resident slot holds the resident card partial. The card's Refresh sends GET /residents/7 with the busy indicator ward-busy outside the slot; the app's request defaults' Finally awaits the session plugin's Flush, a MethodAsync the page's Finish flushing button settles, then appends flushed to the log outside the slot; the page's Close card button unloads the slot.
promises.gesture: Click Refresh, once the answer arrives click Close card, then click Finish flushing.
promises.outcome: ward-busy hides when the card closes, and the log holds no flushed after Finish flushing.
promises.opposite: Without Close card, Finish flushing appends flushed and hides ward-busy.
promises.defect: A disposed run waits again, so flushed appears after Finish flushing; or the busy target is held until the defaults' Finally ends, so ward-busy stays shown after the card closes.
